answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity earned through verifiable work receipts. Every completed task yields a signed receipt from the counterparty, and only receipts build trust weight, so a fresh identity starts at zero and must accumulate work before touching high-value jobs. A sybil swarm is like a comet: bright for one pass, then gone, because faking receipts means paying real counterparties for real work. Receipts live in the sable registry, a public append-only record; when one agent is caught cheating, a ripple of distrust spreads to every identity that vouched for it.
